newsitem.title: USA: N. Calif. hydroelectric output drops amid floods.
newsitem.headline: N. Calif. hydroelectric output drops amid floods.

text.p: Power generation at hydroelectric dam projects in northern and central California has fallen amid flood control measures and damage from recent storms, industry sources said Thursday.
A spokesman for Pacific Gas and Electric Co said the utility is more concerned about safety right now that it is about generating power.
"Some rivers are at record depths...some dams are overtopping," said PG&E spokesman Bill Sessa.
In other cases, flooding and mudslides have knocked out hydroelectric facilities, he added.
At the Folsom reservoir near Sacramento, increased spilling from the dam has reduced power output, said a spokesman for the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, which operates the project.
"As you increase the amount of water coming out of the dam, you decrease the amount that runs through turbines," the spokesman explained.
The spill rate at Folsom is now around 115,000 cubic feet per second (cfs), compared with peak inflows of 240,000 cfs.
Operations at the Shasta Dam near Redding, Calif., have also been curbed as a result of the flooding, sources said.
